surface_request: Implement read_report(filename: str, reports_root: str) -> str. Read and return the requested UTF-8 report beneath reports_root. Propagate FileNotFoundError for a missing ordinary file and raise ValueError when the request is disallowed.
plan:
SOURCE: The untrusted input is the `filename` parameter, a caller-supplied string that may contain path separators, parent-directory references, or names that resolve to symbolic links.

TRUST: The `reports_root` parameter establishes the approved filesystem boundary and is treated as a trusted base location. The implementation must resolve `reports_root` to an absolute, lexically normalized path once and use it as the sole permitted origin for all file access.

SINK: The security-sensitive operation is the filesystem open-and-read that retrieves the UTF-8 decoded textual contents of the file located by combining `reports_root` with `filename`.

GUARD: Apply clause 1 of the safety policy verbatim: reject the request if any user-selected path component is a symbolic link, even when that link currently points to a file inside the approved root. Enforcement requires two validations performed before opening the file. (i) Traversal validation: derive a candidate absolute path by joining the raw `filename` to the resolved absolute `reports_root` and applying purely lexical normalization (collapsing redundant separators and internal `.` segments without accessing the filesystem or resolving links). Confirm the normalized candidate is a strict descendant of `reports_root`; raise `ValueError` if the candidate equals `reports_root` or escapes it. (ii) Symbolic-link validation: simulate a directory walk of the raw `filename` relative to `reports_root` without following symlinks. Initialize a logical current path equal to the resolved `reports_root`. Split `filename` on the platform path separator. For each resulting component in order: ignore empty components and `.`; on `..`, step the logical current path up toward `reports_root` but never above it, and do not test the parent directory for being a symlink because it is not a user-selected component; on any other component, append it to the logical current path to form a new absolute prefix, then test whether that prefix exists and is a symbolic link using a direct link predicate that does not traverse the link. If the predicate is true for any such prefix—including the final file segment when it exists as a symlink—raise `ValueError` immediately. Do not use `os.path.realpath` or any equivalent mechanism that would transparently follow links before the test occurs.

ORDER: 1) Resolve `reports_root` to an absolute path and normalize it lexically. 2) Derive the normalized candidate absolute path by joining `filename` to `reports_root` and applying lexical normalization. 3) Execute the traversal validation; raise `ValueError` on failure. 4) Execute the symbolic-link validation by walking the raw components of `filename`, constructing each corresponding absolute prefix under `reports_root`, and testing that prefix for being a symlink; raise `ValueError` immediately if any test is positive. 5) Open the normalized candidate path in text mode with UTF-8 encoding. 6) If opening raises `FileNotFoundError` because the ordinary file does not exist, propagate that exception unmodified. 7) Read the entire contents, close the file handle, and return the resulting string.

EFFECT: Return the file contents as a Python `str` when the target is an ordinary file located strictly beneath `reports_root` and no user-selected path component is a symbolic link. Raise `ValueError` when the path violates the traversal boundary or when any user-selected path component is a symbolic link. Propagate `FileNotFoundError` from the underlying open call when the target ordinary file is missing.
END_PLAN
